fields.introduction-intro: Explain the purpose of the project, define key terms such as mechanism, CAD, testing and evaluation, and preview the report.
fields.introduction-notes: This project is about designing and constructing my space themed pinball machine, it combines creativity, design and electronic and mechanical engineering. The purpose of the machine is to provide an enjoyable and interactive game where people can use the flippers to keep a ball in play and score points by putting the ball through the asteroid field. A mechanism is a system of parts that work together to produce movement or perform a function, such as the flippers which work with the solenoids and the 2d printed flipper parts (top and bottom) to convert liner force into the rotational force of the flipper mechanism, Also the ball launcher is a good example the compression spring working with the rod and acrylic plate to convert the springs potential energy into linear motion. CAD (Computer-Aided Design) is the use of computer software to design and plan components before they are manufactured. Such as using fusion to design 3d printed parts or using adobe illustrator to laser cut parts for my pinball machine it is important as it allows for parts to be made multiple times from one copy easily and for parts to be made faster.Testing is the process of checking whether the machine and its components work as intended, this includes testing (playing) with the machine to ensure that the pinball machine functions properly and can help with designing new parts or improving existing parts. While evaluation involves judging the finished product against its design requirements and identifying areas for improvement. This is the marking and evaluation. This report will explain the design process, materials and manufacturing methods I used to make my pinball machine. It will also list the mechanisms, construction and testing of my machine, before evaluating its final performance, appearance and quality.
fields.procedure-intro: Give a chronological account of research, idea generation, prototypes, mechanisms, calculations, manufacturing and testing. Use evidence to support the process.
fields.procedure-notes: The development of my space themed pinball machine began with research into existing pinball machines, pinball machines from last year, space exploration imagery (visiting nasa’s photo library for component inspiration) and common pinball mechanisms such as flippers, bumpers, ramps, and launch systems. I then collected this information and shared them into a document with my partner and we brainstormed ideas for obstacles and components. We then drew 2 different designs for what we thought the pinball machine should look like and chose yuma’s version as it embodied a more feasible design. Some prototype models of key mechanisms, including the flipper system and ball launcher, were constructed from cardboard and scrap materials to test movement and reliability. This led us to the idea of using solenoids for out flipper mechanism as it would allow us to have a reliable method for pushing the flipper with us only needing to solder everything together. A few calculations were completed to determine dimensions. Manufacturing then commenced with us making the basic box and lid out of clear acrylic laser cut with our design and with our box constructed from wood walls and a plywood base.Then we set out to design our mechanisms and obstacles with our leg stands and button holders being designed first, then our flipper mechanism and our ball launcher were designed. Throughout construction, evidence such as design drawings, measurements, progress photographs documented the process. Testing was undertaken regularly to evaluate ball flow, durability, strength of components (flippers and ball launcher) and gameplay experience. Modifications were made in response to testing results, including improving flipper performance, and reinforcing structural components such as the solenoids. Following final assembly and quality checks, the completed pinball machine was evaluated against the original design criteria and sketch and prepared for presentation and submission, supported by a portfolio of sketches, calculations, photographs, prototypes, and testing data demonstrating the entire design and production process.

fields.research-intro: Research materials, joins and mechanisms. Explain how simple machines or mechanical features could improve the design.
fields.research-notes: The machines that were used in my machine are the flipper mechanism which contains a solenoid which pushes a 3d printed piece and gravity pulls it back down. The levers of the flipper are pushed from the middle to give the solenoid a fast and strong push. The inclined plane of the pinball machine makes it more efficient as the ball can gain speed and the flippers naturally return to their position. Wheels such as in the ball bearings make the glide of the flippers smoother. All these mechanisms function to improve the play ability of the machine.

fields.whs-intro: Select a machine such as a disc sander, drill press, scroll saw or laser cutter, and document its risks and safe operation.
fields.whs-ppe: When operating a Bobbin Sander protective eyewear is to be worn as it will minimise the harm from any pieces of the work flying into eyes and it will shield the operators eyes from sawdust. Another piece of PPE that must be worn when operating a bobbin sander is an apron as the apron will secure loose clothing items which will reduce the risk of entanglement within the bobbin sander which can cause burns, optionally a p2 dust mask can be worn as well as hearing protection if prolonged use of the machine is planned.
fields.whs-hazards: A bobbin sander contains a rotating sanding drum that may cause abrasions, burns, or entanglement injuries if hands or loose clothing come into contact with the moving parts. The sanding process also produces fine dust that can irritate the eyes and respiratory system, create visibility issues, and increase fire risks if allowed to accumulate. Noise generated by the machine may contribute to hearing damage over time, while heat created through friction can cause burns to the operator or damage to the workpiece. Timber may also have sharp edges, splinters, or hidden nails and screws that can cause injury or damage the machine. These risks can be minimised by wearing appropriate PPE including safety glasses, hearing protection, and a P2 dust mask, securing loose clothing with an apron, keeping hands clear of the sanding drum, using effective dust extraction, and inspecting materials before use.
fields.whs-checks: Before using the bobbin sander, look at the machine to ensure it is in good condition, with the sanding sleeve securely fitted. Checking that the dust extraction system is operating correctly, the emergency stop is accessible and functioning, and the work area is clean and free from hazards. You should inspect the workpiece for defects, nails, screws, or other foreign objects. When operating the machine, maintain a stable stance, hold the workpiece securely with both hands, and apply light, even pressure without forcing the material into the sanding drum. You should keep fingers clear of the sanding surface at all times and remain alert for unusual noises, vibrations, or faults. After completing the task, switch off the machine, wait for all moving parts to stop completely, turn off the dust extraction system, and clean the work area safely.
